notes:
Input locators and neutral description are empty. The named replication report independently identifies a single-trace claim and original Table 3 column (1) in paragraph 9. Original full paper was not acquired; original statistics quoted by the replication report were not substituted for primary original evidence. Original acquisition routes and failures are recorded in texts/6a6805dd9458d065873626f8.miss. Replication es_type ser_method is not a printed effect metric; the printed regression coefficient is retained without conversion (standard error 0.151). Main replication uses new data and differs in growth-window availability and country coverage from the original; robustness estimates in paragraphs 17 and 20 are separate tests and were not combined. Replication exclusions are not documented; reported 77 observations are explicitly attached to the target regression.
Source follow-up: Fresh original-only validation. Assigned original locator is empty, study_o and description are null, and es_type_o is null. The replication reference does not identify an original regression coefficient or model. Supplied published full text matches the assigned title, authors, DOI and article pagination (54–69). Rendered PDF page 10 (printed p. 63), Table 3, was visually inspected: it contains eight model columns with differing coefficients and observation/country counts. Tables 4 (p. 65) and 6 (pp. 68–69) contain additional distinct tests. No unique target can be selected from these alternatives without inventing a locator; all target statistics therefore remain null. Paper is available; locator insufficiency does not imply source unavailability. Source version is the published article; appendix begins on printed p. 68, within continuous article pagination. Reported success was not extracted because the assigned target is original only.
